interest: For historians of Japanese foreign relations, interwar migration, and U.S.-Japan diplomacy, this file provides a valuable strategic roadmap to the State Department's monitoring of Japanese global emigration during the 1930s. The docket entries illustrate the geopolitical interplay between Japan's continental expansion in East Asia and its overseas migration to Latin America, documenting how the recognized difficulties and climatic barriers to mass colonization in Manchuria led Tokyo to vigorously promote emigration to Brazil, Peru, and Paraguay. The records also illuminate growing American official anxiety regarding Japanese demographic and commercial penetration in the Western Hemisphere, highlighted by high-level memoranda prepared directly for President Franklin D. Roosevelt and intelligence assessments by the War Department. Furthermore, the file documents the legal evolution of Japanese emigration policy examined by the Treaty Division since 1896 and charts the escalation toward aggressive state-directed settlement schemes, notably the 1937 twenty-year plan to settle five million Japanese in Manchukuo.
overview: This file constitutes decimal file 894.56, titled 'Japan, Emigration' (File 570), from the U.S. State Department's Records Relating to Internal Affairs of Japan, covering October 1930 through May 1939. It comprises four sheets of the Department's 'List of Papers' docket sheets (Sheet 1, Page 4, Page 5, and Sheet 6) indexing incoming and outgoing diplomatic despatches, consular reports, inter-departmental memoranda, military attaché reports, foreign diplomatic notes, and public inquiries regarding Japanese emigration and overseas settlement. The indexed documents trace the evolution of Japanese emigration policy during the 1930s, documenting agricultural settlement and colonization in Brazil, Peru, Paraguay, Mexico, the Philippines, the Dutch East Indies, and the South Seas Mandate, alongside planned settlement projects in Manchuria (Manchukuo) following the 1931 Mukden Incident and the eventual realization of the difficulties of mass settlement on the Asian mainland. The file also reflects American official monitoring of Japanese commercial penetration in Latin America—including memoranda prepared for President Franklin D. Roosevelt—and legal reviews of Japanese emigration restrictions dating back to 1896. Because almost all underlying substantive records were cross-referenced and filed under country-specific classifications (notably 832.5594 for Brazil and 893.5594 for Manchuria), this file serves as a comprehensive central index to prewar American diplomatic intelligence on Japanese migratory movements.

subfiles.about: List of papers docket sheet indexing State Department records and cross-references on Japanese emigration from October 1930 to May 1931.
subfiles.summary: This docket sheet indexes State Department documentation under decimal file 894.56 from October 1930 through May 1931 (sub-numbers 57 through 64). Entries include consular and diplomatic reporting from São Paulo, Tokyo, and Lima regarding Japanese population statistics abroad, emigration discrepancies in Peru, and migration to the Philippines, Dutch East Indies, Federated Malay States, and the Japanese Mandate Islands. It also indexes several letters of inquiry from American citizens concerning Japanese movement into South American countries, along with the Department's official replies.
subfiles.title: List of Papers: Emigration from Japan (Sheet 1, Sub-numbers 57–64)

subfiles.about: List of papers docket sheet indexing State Department records and cross-references on Japanese emigration from August 1932 to April 1934.
subfiles.summary: This docket sheet indexes documentation recorded between August 1932 and April 1934 (sub-numbers 65 through 73). It details proposed plans for settling Japanese ex-servicemen in Manchuria, a project to send 10,000 Japanese emigrants to Brazil, and Treaty Division legal memoranda reviewing Japanese emigration restrictions since 1896. It also covers consular and military attaché reports from Kobe, Harbin, and Tokyo highlighting the redirection of Japanese emigration toward South America following the realization of the impracticability of mass colonization in Manchuria.
subfiles.title: List of Papers: Emigration from Japan (Page 4, Sub-numbers 65–73)

subfiles.about: List of papers docket sheet indexing State Department records and cross-references on Japanese emigration from May 1934 to December 1938.
subfiles.summary: This docket sheet indexes State Department records from May 1934 through December 1938 (sub-numbers 74 through 80). It includes Division of Latin-American Affairs reports and a memorandum prepared for President Franklin D. Roosevelt on Japanese migration to Brazil and Peru, as well as an invitation from the President of Paraguay requesting Japanese settlers. It also indexes a War Department report on Japanese commercial penetration in Latin America, a 1937 military attaché report detailing Japan's twenty-year plan to settle five million colonists in Manchukuo, and a 1938 report on Japanese immigration to the Philippines.
subfiles.title: List of Papers: Emigration from Japan (Page 5, Sub-numbers 74–80)

subfiles.about: List of papers docket sheet recording Japanese Embassy Note No. 106 transmitting Home Department Ordinance No. 6.
subfiles.summary: This docket sheet indexes sub-number 81 in decimal file 894.56, entered on May 11, 1939. It records Note No. 106 from the Japanese Embassy in Washington, which transmitted an English translation of Japanese Home Department Ordinance No. 6. The original paper was cross-referenced and filed under decimal file 894.111/78.
subfiles.title: List of Papers: Emigration from Japan (Sheet 6, Sub-number 81)
